title: Canonical publication observables corpus (RUB-922 / C01), schema version 1
description: Machine contract for conformance/fixtures/protocol/canonical_pipeline_v1.json, the sole external authority for canonical-pipeline results and effects. It constrains observable old-or-new publication, exact first-error and result identity, bounded resource outcomes and effect counts, and never names a mutex, an internal struct or a client-private type. An omitted optional row field states no expectation: it is neither a zero nor a wildcard match. Ordered sequences carried as strings list their elements in document order, separated by ', ' (or by '; ' where an element itself contains a comma).

authority.description: Provenance of every expected value: the architecture parent as superseded, the pinned normative spec and repository baselines, the executors that may consume this artifact, and the frozen consume direction. Expected rows are authored architecture authority; the generator never calls a node production path to compute one.

result_taxonomy.description: The closed result taxonomy. Every observation row result is a member name, optionally followed by its exact parenthesized argument.

coverage_receipt.description: Generated receipt mapping every enumerated class (closed result taxonomy plus every named observable, accepted, rejected and hostile bullet of RUB-922) to the row ids that define it. A class mapping to no row is a generation failure, never a corpus state.

canonical_counters.description: Exact planner-owned canonical counter deltas as exact decimal or symbolic tokens, for example '+1', '0' or '+connect_count'.

pending_owner.description: NORMATIVE ACCEPTANCE SEMANTICS. A row carrying pending_owner names the RUB issue that must deliver the machinery the row describes. Until that issue is Done the row is excluded from the RUB-926 zero-mismatch acceptance comparison and from RUB-901 Go-versus-Rust equality: an adapter MUST still emit whatever it observes for the row, and a comparator MUST NOT report the row as a mismatch. When the named issue is Done the field is removed by a C01 revision and the row becomes gate-bearing. Only RUB-922 (C01) may add, change or remove this field; a consumer that mutates it is out of contract.
